data.narrative:
Flapping Airplanes is a private AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage with three founders (Benjamin Spector, Asher Spector, Aidan Smith). The valuation universe for peer analysis consists of 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. Despite identifying 12 same-sector AI & Software peers, none satisfied the filtering criteria required for reliable triangulation: no peers matched both the target's stage and valuation tier simultaneously, and fewer than three datapoints remained after applying same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier screens. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise and misrepresent the target's positioning within narrower peer brackets.

Without a sufficiently robust peer set and lacking disclosed financials (revenue, growth rate, profitability margins) or transaction multiples from the identified private comparables, this analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range at this time. The primary constraint is data scarcity: the private peer set is underpowered for statistical inference, and public comparables (Palantir alone) do not form a representative anchor for an early-stage or mid-stage private company. A valuation conclusion would require either disclosure of the target's stage and key metrics, or access to multiples and financial detail from the private peer cohort.
